turnos.t: Why does limited liability matter so much?

A company is a separate legal person. It can own assets, sign contracts, sue and be sued. So its shareholders have limited liability: they can only lose the money they invested, and their personal assets are protected.
How does that help the business?
Because investors only risk what they put in, more people are willing to buy shares. The company raises more capital, and can grow faster than a sole trader.
